storyboard.claim: The island is being consumed by Diem's unleashed magic in a white-hot blaze.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A scorched landscape burning under a silver-white fire icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the temple battle sequence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the fire a colour and a scale: an island-wide inferno, not a campfire.
storyboard.staging: Fire icon over the burning forest, no people: the blaze is the subject.

explainedBy: The sentence names a group of immortal beings; a single figure would misrepresent a group and a crowd repeats one person, so the callout names them.
noVisual: A group of godlike immortals has no vocabulary icon, and a crowd shot would repeat one person as ghost duplicates.

storyboard.claim: The kindred are ancient immortal beings who shaped the world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No figure; the callout names the group against the fire.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the fire of the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Who the kindred are.

explainedBy: Diem listens while the kindred confess a sin to her: she is the one hearing the confession.

storyboard.claim: The kindred weep and confess their sin to Diem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Diem standing, head slightly lowered, listening with a troubled look.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The kindred are introduced in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The kindred confess to Diem, not to the audience.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred built the temple on Corel out of god stone, with no malice intended.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The temple on Corel where the god stone was used.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the origin of the god stone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the object the temple is built from: the god stone.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with the callout naming the god stone temple.

explainedBy: A child's hand is cut on the god stone: this injury is the first event that reveals the stone is dangerous.
noVisual: No child figure is in the cast and no icon reads literally as a cut.

storyboard.claim: A child cut his hand on the god stone, starting the discovery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No figure; the callout names the injury.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the monument intention.
storyboard.addedInformation: The accident that started the discovery.

explainedBy: The Kindred learn the material is toxic: the injury is the cause, and the lethal material is the effect they discover.
noVisual: Toxicity has no icon; the callout states the property.

storyboard.claim: The god stone is highly toxic and lethal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No figure; the callout states the lethal property.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the child's injury.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stone's toxicity is the discovery.

storyboard.claim: The monument, built to honour the children, was lethal to them: a murder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon over the temple, read as death.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lethal material is applied to the Kindred's own children.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grave reads the lethal result literally: death.
storyboard.staging: Grave icon over the temple stage with the callout naming the murder.

storyboard.claim: The worst atrocities start from desperate attempts to protect the people you love, not from malice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon, the literal sense of protection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the Kindred's panic into a truth about conflict.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shield states the motive, protection, without the word malice.
storyboard.staging: Shield icon on an abstract set with the callout stating the motive.

storyboard.claim: Hiding a catastrophic mistake guarantees the children will have to fight the war.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon, the consequence the children inherit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the panic to the cost of burying a mistake.
storyboard.addedInformation: War makes the consequence literal: the children fight it.
storyboard.staging: War icon with the callout on the act of hiding sins.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred erased the mistake from the minds of the whole continent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A puppeteer icon: one power controlling many minds.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Escalates from burying the mistake to erasing it from every mind.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puppeteer shows control over others, which is what the erasing does.
storyboard.staging: Puppeteer icon with the callout on the erasure.

storyboard.claim: Umbrose magic, which works on shadows in the mind, wiped the memory of Ofuca and the stone's danger from everyone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract set with the magic named in the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the method of the erasure.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: no icon reads shadow-magic literally; the callout names the method.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with callout; no icon, so no false reading.

storyboard.claim: Wiping the memory of an entire continent is a massive violation of autonomy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract set with the verdict named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator stops to judge the method.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the moral judgement directly.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with the verdict callout.

explainedBy: The wipe removes choices from the people it erases: their autonomy is taken, which is the consequence the narration names.
noVisual: Autonomy has no icon that reads literally; the callout names it.

storyboard.claim: Erasing history is a violation of autonomy, and the Kindred erased their own brother.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No figure; the callout names the violation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Judges the wipe from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Kindred erased their own brother from history.

explainedBy: Fear is the cause: the Kindred fear that mortals would harvest the stone and kill the children, so they alter reality.
noVisual: Terror has no picture here and no figure is staged; the callout states the fear.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred were terrified mortals would harvest godstone and kill the vulnerable children.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No figure; the callout states the fear.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the motive for the wipe.
storyboard.addedInformation: The motive behind the cover-up.

storyboard.claim: The mistake, and the cover-up, are unforgivable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract set with the verdict on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts agree on the verdict.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the hosts' verdict in the narrator's words.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with the verdict callout.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred played God with millions of minds to cover up a monumental mistake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An abstract set with the accusation named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the verdict into the charge of control.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puppeteer was avoided here to keep the accusation from reading as a literal puppet show.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with the accusation callout.

explainedBy: Diem's horror follows the confession: she hears the same sin she committed herself.

storyboard.claim: Diem is horrified because she realises she did the same thing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Diem with a horrified, afraid look, thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the Kindred to Diem.
storyboard.addedInformation: Diem's own parallel act.

storyboard.claim: Diem did the same thing: when Luther was dying of god stone poisoning, she acted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther fallen on the floor, eyes shut, from the poisoning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recalls the earlier scene where Luther was poisoned.
storyboard.addedInformation: Collapsed reads as fallen and dying, not as treatment.
storyboard.staging: Luther collapsed on the floor, sad: the dying man Diem is recalling.

storyboard.claim: Diem vowed never to harm mortals, but at the brink of death she did.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther fallen on the floor again, at the brink of death.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Luther memory with Diem's vow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Repeats the collapse so the viewer links the vow to Luther's fall.
storyboard.staging: Luther collapsed, sad, with the callout on the brink of death.

callout.text: Sank a blade into mortal flesh

explainedBy: Diem's own act: she sank a blade into a mortal, and that act is what saved Luther.

storyboard.claim: Diem actively sank a blade into mortal flesh to save Luther.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Diem slumped, guilty and worried.
storyboard.onScreenText: Sank a blade into mortal flesh
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the act that broke the vow.
storyboard.addedInformation: The act that broke her code.

storyboard.claim: When the person you are bonded to is in danger, you will do terrible things.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heart icon for the bond, read as love.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises Diem's act into a rule about bonds.
storyboard.addedInformation: Heart marks the bond as love, which is the reason for the act.
storyboard.staging: Heart icon with the callout on the bonded person.

storyboard.claim: Her love made her as monstrous as the Kindred.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heart icon for love.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the parallel with the Kindred.
storyboard.addedInformation: Love is the cause named in the callout; monstrous is the verdict.
storyboard.staging: Heart icon with the callout on love and monstrosity.

storyboard.claim: The forging spell that created the realms of Amaran is revealed as the ultimate twisted bond.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon over the realm horizon, read as bound.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the forging spell, the grandest magic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read literally as bound, which is the bond the narrator means.
storyboard.staging: Chains icon over the realm horizon with the callout on the twisted bond.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred chained their magic to the soil, and chained their own souls with it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon on an abstract set, bound.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the cost of the chaining.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains reads bound; the callout says the souls are the bound thing.
storyboard.staging: Chains icon with callout on the Kindred's souls.

storyboard.claim: The Kindred are trapped in endless purgatory between life and death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Grave icon on an abstract set, read as death.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes what the chaining did to the Kindred.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grave reads the death side of purgatory; the callout names the in-between.
storyboard.staging: Grave icon with callout on the state between life and death.

storyboard.claim: Mortals die and move on, but the Kindred could not follow, so they anchored to the living world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Abstract set with the limitation named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reason for the chaining.
storyboard.addedInformation: Explains why the Kindred anchored themselves to the living world.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with the callout on the Kindred's limit.

storyboard.claim: Their desperate, clinging love created a cage for the entire continent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Abstract set with the cage named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the bond into the cage it became.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains were avoided here: the metaphor would read as links rather than confinement.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with the callout on the cage.

storyboard.claim: The different types of bonds show up in the chaos at the temple.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The temple stage with the chaos named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the theory of bonds to the battle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the next argument at the temple.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with callout on the chaos.

storyboard.claim: The Meos king is hypnotized by the heart stone and hurls water magic with dead eyes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Temple stage with the king's state named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the first victim of the heart stone.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the king is not in the cast; the callout names his state.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with callout on the hypnosis.

explainedBy: The king's magic is water: the hurled blasts are the event, and the dead eyes are the effect of the heart stone.

storyboard.claim: The king hurls hissing blasts of water magic while mindless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A water icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the king controlled.
storyboard.addedInformation: The water magic and the dead eyes.

storyboard.claim: Ofus effortlessly shields hundreds of mortals, treating a crown like a toy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Shield icon on the temple stage, read as protection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows Ofus's control in action.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shield reads as protection, which is what Ofus performs.
storyboard.staging: Shield icon with callout on the shielding.

storyboard.claim: His magical aura never flickers, a terrifying display of effortless power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Temple stage with the display named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the aura before the mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the display; no aura can be drawn.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with callout on the display.

storyboard.claim: He is not inspiring loyalty; he hijacks the nervous system through the heart stone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Puppeteer icon: one power controlling others.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the mechanism behind the display.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puppeteer shows control; the negation of loyalty is carried by the callout.
storyboard.staging: Puppeteer icon with callout on forced subjugation.

explainedBy: The sentence poses a question; nothing visual is caused by it, so the callout alone labels the question.
noVisual: A philosophical question has no picture in the vocabulary; the callout states it.

storyboard.claim: The effective control raises a philosophical question about power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No figure; the callout names the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the mechanism to the question.
storyboard.addedInformation: The question itself.

storyboard.claim: True power is not about controlling others like chess pieces.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Abstract set with the rejected phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects control as the source of power.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the phrase the narrator rejects.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with the struck phrase, no figure staged controlling.

storyboard.claim: Forced loyalty breaks the moment the spell drops or the fear wanes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow: spell drops, fear wanes, brittle.
storyboard.onScreenText: FORCED LOYALTY BREAKS WHEN FEAR WANES
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the question to the structure of brittle control.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the cause-effect chain of brittle control visible.
storyboard.staging: Flow diagram of the three steps of brittle control.

callout.text: She takes the rose bane petal

explainedBy: Diem reaches to take the rose bane petal: the action shows the poison in her hand.

storyboard.claim: Diem takes the velvety rose bane petal, the poison.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Diem reaching, holding a flower petal.
storyboard.onScreenText: She takes the rose bane petal
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recalls an earlier action.
storyboard.addedInformation: The poison is the rose bane petal.

storyboard.claim: She knows the danger and swallows it anyway, and she is not being mind controlled.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Abstract set with the rejected phrase struck through.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the control reading of Diem's act.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the mind-control reading; no icon, since puppeteer would show control.
storyboard.staging: Abstract set with struck callout; no figure is staged as controlled.

explainedBy: Diem accepts agonizing pain for the greater good: the pain is the cost she chooses.

storyboard.claim: She acts on blind faith and endures agonizing pain for the greater good.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Diem slumped, sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the sacrifice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cost she accepts.

storyboard.claim: The hosts now argue the opposing side for a moment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Temple stage with the turn named on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the counterargument that Ofus is superior.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the counterargument to come.
storyboard.staging: Temple stage with the devil's advocate callout.
